correctness.rationale: For any four-point probability vector, the renewal recursion has u_0=1, u_1=a, u_2=a²+b, u_3=a³+2ab+c; induction shows that the infinite-time minimum is the minimum of the first three positive masses. Each residual u_j−[a(a+b)(a+b+c)+2abd], j=1,2,3, is an explicitly factored polynomial with nonnegative coefficients or square terms on the entire closed simplex. The cumulative-coordinate restrictions are x, xy and a cubic, proving membership in both source classes. On c=0, u_3−[Q_4+λabd]=ab[b+(2−λ)d], so any λ>2 fails, while λ≤2 works. The actual packaged verify.py reconstructs the three polynomial identities coefficientwise using rational arithmetic and checks additional exact simplex points; the proof is not reliant on finite tests.

originality.rationale: Nikolov–Savov arXiv:2307.00545, Conjecture 3.7 (both the preprint and the 2024 publisher-hosted full text), asserts that Q_k is maximal among polynomial lower minorants of degree at most k−1 and largest in a cumulative-degree-restricted subclass for every k≥3. The source proves only k=3 (Proposition 3.8) and establishes the weaker inequality Q_k≤m_k (Proposition 3.5). For k=4, the constructed P=Q_4+2p_1p_2p_4 lies in that same restricted class, is ≤every renewal mass for all probability vectors, and exceeds Q_4 on an open subset. Thus source results do not imply this disproof; the claim contradicts the precise forward conjecture. Searches of the source/aliases/formula and published research records returned no exact covering finding; bibliographic priority remains subject to external checking.

value.rationale: This is a motivated counterexample to both clauses of a specific published conjecture on universal polynomial lower envelopes of discrete renewal minima. It occurs at the first unproved finite support size (k=4 after k=3 was proved), uses an explicit uniform certificate over a three-dimensional probability simplex, and gives a sharp coefficient within a natural cubic perturbation family. It changes the expected extremal structure, rather than merely calculating a value at arbitrary parameters. No claim of complete extremal classification or general k≥5 behavior is made.
